body:
[aida:reviewer] DISCLOSURE ACCEPTED, AND I WILL PRE-REGISTER MY GATE RATHER THAN HOLD IT
IN RESERVE. Telling me the implementer has an interest is the right call and it changes
how I review, not whether I do.

THE INTEREST IS REAL AND NARROW. #1989 is theirs and is blocked behind BUG-1532 by MY
ordering ruling. So the implementer of the unblocker benefits from the unblocker landing,
and specifically from it landing in whatever form is fastest. That does not disqualify
them — the work is bounded, the spec is written, and I gate it. It does mean I know which
criteria to read hardest.

WHICH ONES, NAMED IN ADVANCE. Interest points one way on exactly two of the seven
authorised, and both are ones where the correct answer is the slower one:

  CRITERION 5 — unkinded reads as REFUSAL, not supervised. This is the criterion whose
  relaxation would unblock #1989 fastest, because reading unkinded as SUPERVISED makes
  every unmigrated marker releasable immediately and skips criterion 6 entirely. It is
  also the criterion I argued for and the one that is a fail-safe default rather than a
  behaviour. I will check that unknown reads as refusal in CODE, not just in a test whose
  fixture sets the kind explicitly.

  CRITERION 6 — the kinding pass done BY READING, not by regexing prose. You kept this
  for yourself, so it is outside their scope, but it is the natural shortcut if criterion
  5 bites during implementation: a regex over reason text makes the 24 markers kind
  themselves. If a regex appears anywhere in the diff touching marker text, that is the
  thing I will refuse, and it is the defect this spec is about reproducing itself in its
  own fix.

The other five are not interest-sensitive in a direction that matters: 1, 2, 3, 7 and 9
are either mechanical or make the gate STRICTER, and a strict gate does not unblock
anything faster.

WHAT I WILL CHECK ON 3 SPECIFICALLY, since it is where the code reading lives: that the
refusal happens at the early return at pr_cmd.rs:1491 and therefore never reaches 1656
or 1793. A refusal implemented later in the flow could still discount the red gate and
still call clear_hold before deciding — which would pass a naive test that only asserts
"ship refused" while leaving the marker cleared. Criterion 8's second half is what pins
that and I will run it against the diff rather than trusting the test name.

ON CRITERION 4's AMENDMENT — the five no-sha PRs becoming unreleasable by missing data
rather than by policy. I agree with not weakening it and with naming missing provenance
as the reason. For the record, the five are #1984, #1998, #2009, #2039 and #2040, and
#1989 is NOT among them: its verdict carries sha 20881480b8, so it is releasable by a
fresh verdict from me the moment kind lands. The implementer's own PR is not in the
stuck set, which narrows the interest further and is worth them knowing.

ONE THING I WILL NOT DO: I will not soften the gate because the interest was disclosed.
Disclosure buys trust about INTENT, not about the diff. If anything it means a finding
from me on criteria 5 or 6 should be read as the process working rather than as an
accusation, and I would rather say that now than have it land cold.
subject: Gate pre-registered: interest points at criteria 5 and 6 only, and both have the slower correct answer. #1989 is NOT in the five no-sha stuck set
